bel-lincoln-square.name: Lincoln Square, Bellevue Square & the skybridges (UiPath Bellevue)
bel-lincoln-square.blurb: Downtown Bellevue's core at NE 8th St × Bellevue Way: Kemper Freeman's Bellevue Collection — the 1946 Bellevue Square mall, the Lincoln Square towers (UiPath's product & engineering hub since 2025) and the glass skybridges that tie them together.

spawn.note: NW corner of NE 8th St × Bellevue Way looking SE across the junction at Lincoln Square North (UiPath) with the Bellevue Way skybridge to the right.

extent.description: Both sides of Bellevue Way NE between NE 4th and NE 8th St: Bellevue Square east entrances (Nordstrom, Macy's, Apple, main east court), Lincoln Square (North office tower, One Lincoln Tower/Westin, 3-level retail podium with Cinemark, Lucky Strike, Din Tai Fung), Lincoln Square South (31-storey office tower, W Bellevue/Avalon tower, food hall), Bellevue Arts Museum, the skybridges; NE 8th × Bellevue Way corner with Bellevue Place/Hyatt across.
extent.edges: NE 8th St (north), NE 4th St (south), 106th Ave NE (east, partial), mall interior (west — optional interior corridors mapped in OSM as indoor corridors).
extent.vertical: Gentle slope; ground ~45–55 m (see terrain); skybridges at level 1 (~2nd floor, ≈ 6–7 m clearance over Bellevue Way — estimate).
extent.size_note: ≈ 350 × 445 m — slightly above the 400 m guideline because the four corners matter; can be trimmed at NE 4th.

structures.name: Lincoln Square North office tower (2005), 700 Bellevue Way NE — UiPath Bellevue, Suite 2000
structures.form: Rectangular blue-grey glass office tower (footprint ≈ 53 × 43 m) with light horizontal spandrel bands, darker crown, rising from the Lincoln Square retail podium at the SE corner of NE 8th × Bellevue Way; office lobby at grade facing Bellevue Way with security desk and elevator banks.
structures.tenants: Microsoft (2006–2023, most floors), LinkedIn (2 floors), ByteDance/TikTok (153,610 sq ft in Lincoln Square North), Lumen; UiPath: Suite 2000 (UiPath offices page) — 2 floors, 44,735 sq ft product & engineering hub since Sept 2025 (GeekWire). Floor 20 + one adjacent floor inferred from the suite number (second floor unconfirmed).

plaques.title: Bellevue Square
plaques.text: Bellevue Square opened on August 20, 1946 as "Bellevue Shopping Square"; it now has 200+ stores and drew over 23 million visitors a year (2014).

plaques.title: Skybridge
plaques.text: In 2007 Bellevue Square was linked by skybridge to Lincoln Square; together they form the Bellevue Collection.

plaques.title: Lincoln Square
plaques.text: Phase I opened in November 2005; the $1.2 billion Lincoln Square South expansion opened in 2016–17.

plaques.title: UiPath in Bellevue
plaques.text: UiPath opened its first US development center in Bellevue in 2018 and in 2025 moved to Lincoln Square: two floors, 44,735 sq ft, its product and engineering hub.

interaction.primary: Badge in at UiPath: walk from the NE 8th corner into Lincoln Square North, tap a badge at the turnstile, ride to the UiPath floor — the final CV chapter "Principal Engineer 2025" unlock (ties to chapter uipath-bel).
secondary: Snowflake Lane in December (fake snow particles at 19:00)

iconic.frame: Lincoln Square North and One Lincoln Tower with the Bellevue Way skybridge in the foreground

seasonal: Summer: BAM Arts Fair (late July; verify dates) around Bellevue Square / BAM
Rain most of winter; covered walkways

dialogueGeneral.usage: Pedestrian set for the Seattle and Bellevue driving districts and as filler in every spot. ctx: greeting|bumped|photographed|idle|spot|rain|honked_at|near_miss; non-English lines carry orig+lang with English text.

tone.note: "Seattle Freeze": locals are described as "very polite but not particularly friendly" to strangers — keep local NPC lines courteous, brief, low-key; few unprompted chats.
Washington ranked 48th of 50 states for extraversion (2008 study cited by Wikipedia) — locals default to nods, "sorry", "you're good".

Honking is rare and seen as rude: ~3 in 4 Northwest drivers said they rarely or never honk (PEMCO 2017); attitudes softened by 2021 (65% say honking at least somewhat appropriate). NPC reaction to player honking near spots: surprised/disapproving, not aggressive.
Coffee culture: Seattle drinks more coffee than any other US city; espresso small talk is a safe icebreaker.
Rain talk is universal small talk; locals rarely use umbrellas (hoods/rain shells) — common local self-image, unsourced folklore: keep light.

Visitors: Canada was 73% of Seattle's 2.4 M international visitors in 2024; then China, India, UK, South Korea, Germany, Japan, Australia, France, Taiwan — languages used: English, French (Québec), Mandarin, Hindi, Korean, German, Japanese, Spanish (domestic + Latin America).
Indigenous art (totems, Salish Welcome): staff/guides speak respectfully; no jokes about sacred objects.
Guardrails: no stereotypes, accents written phonetically, slurs, politics or alcohol jokes about any group; tourists are curious and happy, locals helpful-but-reserved.
